newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends steadier on Tokyo's gains.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends steadier on Tokyo's gains.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended steadier in quiet trading after a higher Tokyo market and expectation of some fresh European demand, dealers said.
"The market is holding steady because of Tokyo. There weren't much happening from Asian buyers but we expect some fresh enquiries from Europe after the summer holidays," one dealer said.
"Factories are expected to resume operations and they need the raw materials," he said.
"Supply situation is a bit tight and producers are holding back their stocks while waiting for higher levels."
Intermittent rains in Malaysia and other producing countries had limited tapping activities, dealers said.
"We expect the Europeans to make fresh enquiries for latex rubber and SMR grades," a dealer said.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board set indicator price for Oct RSS1 buyer at 328 cents ($1.31) a kg, up half a cent. Oct SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 313.50 cents.
The INRO five-day average was 251.48 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 10 from 252.08 on Sept 9. The daily indicator price was 250.20 cents against 250.32.
